name: Cappadocia · Göreme
tagline: Fairy chimneys, cave churches and balloons at dawn
summary: Base yourself in Göreme and walk to the open-air museum and the valleys. Give one dawn to the balloons, one day to the valleys on foot and one to an underground city and the Ihlara gorge.
seasonNote: Winters are snowy and cold and balloons are often grounded by wind; July and August are hot and dry.
arrival: Fly to Kayseri (1 hour away) or Nevşehir (40 minutes) and book a shared shuttle to your hotel in advance; overnight buses run from Istanbul.
gettingAround: Göreme is walkable and the valleys start at its edge. Local buses link Göreme, Uçhisar, Avanos and Ürgüp; the far sights need a tour or rental car.
cashTip: Museums price tickets in euros but take cards in lira; carry lira for village buses, tea gardens and small cafes.
foodTip: Order testi kebabı, a stew sealed and baked in a clay pot, along with mantı dumplings and gözleme flatbread.
buyTip: Avanos is the pottery town; carpets and onyx are sold everywhere, so compare before buying.
baseArea: Göreme for walking access; Uçhisar for quiet and views

connections.note: To Kayseri or Nevşehir, plus an hour's shuttle.
Overnight bus; no direct flights most of the year.

items.name: Göreme Open Air Museum
items.summary: A cluster of rock-cut monastery churches with Byzantine frescoes from the 10th to 12th centuries.
items.expect: Tour groups fill the small churches from mid-morning; photos are not allowed inside.
items.tip: Arrive at opening and pay the extra fee for the Dark Church, which has the best-preserved frescoes.
items.why: It is the clearest look at why monks carved this landscape and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
flow: Walk 20 minutes uphill from Göreme.
Circle the churches clockwise, ending at the Dark Church.

items.name: Sunrise hot air balloon flight
items.summary: An hour drifting over the valleys with a hundred other balloons at first light.
items.expect: A pickup around 5 am; flights are cancelled on windy days, most often in winter.
items.tip: Book for your first morning so you can rebook if the wind cancels it.
items.why: It is the experience Cappadocia is known for and the view explains the whole landscape.
flow: Hotel pickup before dawn.
One hour in the air, then a short landing toast.

items.name: Uçhisar Castle
items.summary: A hollowed rock citadel at the highest point of the region, with a view over every valley.
items.expect: A steep climb on uneven steps; busy at sunset.
items.tip: Walk down afterwards through Pigeon Valley back to Göreme, about an hour.
items.why: The best wide view in Cappadocia for a small fee.
flow: Bus or taxi from Göreme, 10 minutes.
Climb to the top, then walk Pigeon Valley.

items.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
items.summary: A city dug eight levels down, with stables, chapels and ventilation shafts, that once sheltered thousands.
items.expect: Low, narrow tunnels; not for anyone uneasy in tight spaces.
items.tip: Go early or late to avoid queues in the one-way passages.
items.why: The deepest of the region's underground cities and unlike anything above ground.
flow: 40 minutes by car or tour south of Göreme.
Follow the arrows down and back up.

items.name: Zelve Open Air Museum and Paşabağ
items.summary: An abandoned cave village in three valleys, next to Paşabağ's mushroom-capped fairy chimneys.
items.expect: Fewer visitors than Göreme's museum and more freedom to explore.
items.tip: One ticket covers both sites; start at Paşabağ before the buses arrive.
items.why: The best place to see fairy chimneys close up.
flow: Avanos bus from Göreme or a short taxi.
Paşabağ first, then walk the Zelve valleys.

items.name: Rose and Red Valley sunset walk
items.summary: Trails through pink and ochre rock past hidden chapels to a ridge that glows at sunset.
items.expect: Unmarked forks in the trail; download an offline map.
items.tip: Start from Çavuşin two hours before sunset and finish at the Red Valley viewpoint.
items.why: The finest walk in the park and it is free.
flow: Taxi or bus to Çavuşin.
Walk up to the sunset viewpoint, then down to Göreme.

items.name: Ihlara Valley
items.summary: A green river gorge lined with painted rock churches, an hour and a half from Göreme.
items.expect: About 400 steps down; the full walk is 14 km, though most do a 4 km section.
items.tip: The 'Green Tour' combines the valley with Derinkuyu and Selime Monastery in one day.
items.why: A cool, shaded contrast to the dry valleys around Göreme.
flow: Join a Green Tour or drive 90 minutes.
Walk from the Ihlara entrance to Belisırma for lunch by the river.

items.name: Dibek
items.summary: A family restaurant in a 475-year-old stone house with floor cushions and low tables.
items.expect: Testi kebabı must be ordered three hours ahead.
items.tip: Reserve in the morning and order the clay-pot kebab at the same time.
items.why: The most traditional setting in Göreme for the region's signature dish.
flow: Reserve and pre-order.
Shoes off; the pot is cracked open at the table.

items.name: Topdeck Cave Restaurant
items.summary: A small cave dining room run by a chef and his family, serving a short daily menu.
items.expect: Only a handful of tables; closed some days.
items.tip: Book a day or two ahead and share the meze plate.
items.why: Consistently the most recommended dinner in Göreme.
flow: Reserve ahead.
Meze to share, then a slow-cooked main.

items.name: Bizim Ev
items.summary: A terraced restaurant in the pottery town of Avanos, known for clay-pot dishes.
items.expect: Popular with tour lunches; quieter in the evening.
items.tip: Pair lunch with a pottery workshop visit by the river.
items.why: A good reason to see Avanos and eat well away from Göreme's main strip.
flow: Bus from Göreme, 15 minutes.
Lunch on the terrace, then the pottery street.

name: Antalya
tagline: Roman harbour, turquoise coast and ruins in the hills
summary: Stay in or near the old town, Kaleiçi, for the harbour and lanes, then use the city as a base for Aspendos, Perge and Termessos. Beaches run along both sides of the city.
seasonNote: July and August reach 35 to 40°C with high humidity; winter is mild and rainy with many beach hotels closed.
arrival: Antalya airport is 13 km east; the tram reaches the old town in about 40 minutes and taxis take 25.
gettingAround: Kaleiçi is on foot. The tram runs to the museum and the airport; Aspendos, Perge and Termessos are easiest by rental car or tour.
cashTip: Cards work nearly everywhere; keep lira for the tram card, beach loungers and small cafes.
foodTip: Antalya's own dishes are piyaz (bean salad with tahini), şiş köfte and serpme börek; finish with burnt ice cream.
buyTip: Kaleiçi sells leather, spices and Turkish delight; prices drop a street or two back from the harbour.
baseArea: Kaleiçi for atmosphere; Konyaaltı or Lara for a beach hotel
via: Direct from many European cities; otherwise via Istanbul

connections.note: Bus to Denizli, then a minibus.

items.name: Kaleiçi old town and harbour
items.summary: Ottoman houses, Roman walls and a small harbour under the cliffs.
items.expect: Cobbled lanes, many steps down to the harbour and plenty of touts near the marina.
items.tip: Walk it early or after 5 pm, and take the free panoramic lift back up from the harbour.
items.why: The heart of the city and the reason to stay in Antalya itself.
flow: Enter through Hadrian's Gate.
Wander down to the harbour and up to Karaalioğlu Park for the view.

items.name: Hadrian's Gate
items.summary: A triple marble arch built for the emperor's visit in 130 AD.
items.expect: A quick stop; the grooves of cart wheels are visible under the glass walkway.
items.tip: Pass through at night when it is lit.
items.why: The best-preserved Roman monument inside the city.
flow: Tram to İsmetpaşa.
Walk through into Kaleiçi.

items.name: Antalya Museum
items.summary: One of Turkey's best archaeology museums, with halls of statues from Perge.
items.expect: Air-conditioned and rarely crowded.
items.tip: See it before visiting Perge so the empty niches there make sense.
items.why: The Perge sculpture gallery is world class.
flow: Tram to Müze, the last stop.
Hall of the Gods, then the sarcophagi.

items.name: Aspendos Theatre
items.summary: A Roman theatre for 15,000, so intact that it still hosts opera.
items.expect: Little shade; the climb to the top rows is steep.
items.tip: Combine with Perge on the same drive east.
items.why: The best-preserved Roman theatre anywhere.
flow: 45 minutes by car from Antalya.
Climb to the upper gallery, then walk to the aqueduct.

items.name: Perge
items.summary: A Roman city with a colonnaded main street, a stadium and Hellenistic gate towers.
items.expect: A large open site in full sun.
items.tip: Bring water and a hat; allow time for the stadium outside the gate.
items.why: It shows the layout of a whole Roman city, 20 minutes from Antalya.
flow: Tram to Aksu and a short taxi, or by car.
Stadium, gate, then the long colonnaded street.

items.name: Termessos
items.summary: A ruined mountain city at 1,000 metres with a theatre on the edge of a ravine.
items.expect: A 30-minute uphill hike on rough paths; no facilities.
items.tip: Wear proper shoes and go in the morning; there is no public transport to the top.
items.why: The most dramatic setting of any ancient site near Antalya, and few people go.
flow: 45 minutes by car, then 9 km up the park road.
Hike to the theatre and the rock tombs.

items.name: Lower Düden Waterfall
items.summary: A river dropping 40 metres off the cliff straight into the Mediterranean.
items.expect: A park at the top; the full view is from a boat.
items.tip: Boats from the Kaleiçi harbour reach the falls in about 45 minutes.
items.why: An easy and unusual sight within the city.
flow: Bus or taxi to Düden Park.
Or take a harbour boat for the sea view.

items.name: 7 Mehmet
items.summary: Antalya's classic restaurant since 1937, with a terrace over Konyaaltı beach.
items.expect: A large, polished dining room; smart-casual dress.
items.tip: Reserve a terrace table for sunset.
items.why: The reference for regional Antalya cooking.
flow: Reserve ahead.
Start with piyaz and cold meze, then lamb.

items.name: Börekçi Tevfik
items.summary: A tiny shop making hand-stretched serpme börek since the 1930s.
items.expect: A few stools; it sells out by early afternoon.
items.tip: Go for breakfast and ask for half minced meat, half cheese.
items.why: A local institution for Antalya's own style of börek.
flow: Arrive before noon.
Order by the portion with tea.

items.name: Şişçi Ramazan'ın Yeri
items.summary: A plain grill house serving the Antalya pairing of şiş köfte and tahini piyaz.
items.expect: Shared tables and fast service at lunch.
items.tip: Order köfte and piyaz together, as locals do.
items.why: The simplest way to taste the city's signature lunch.
flow: Walk from the clock tower.
Köfte, piyaz and ayran.

name: Selçuk · Ephesus
summary: Selçuk is the small town beside Ephesus. Give the ruins a full morning, then add the museum, the Basilica of St. John and the hill village of Şirince.
seasonNote: July and August are very hot on the open marble; cruise groups from Kuşadası arrive mid-morning all season.
arrival: Fly to Izmir; the train from the airport reaches Selçuk in about an hour, or take a bus or transfer.
gettingAround: The town is walkable. Minibuses run to Ephesus, Şirince and the beach at Pamucak; the House of the Virgin Mary needs a taxi.
cashTip: Carry lira for minibuses and the Saturday market; sites take cards.
foodTip: Try çöp şiş (small lamb skewers), Aegean herb dishes in olive oil and fruit wine in Şirince.
buyTip: The Saturday market is the place for olives, dried figs and olive-oil soap.
baseArea: Selçuk town centre, near the Basilica of St. John

connections.note: To Izmir, plus an hour by train.
Train or bus to Denizli, then a minibus.

items.name: Ephesus
items.summary: The most complete classical city in the eastern Mediterranean, with the Library of Celsus and a 25,000-seat theatre.
items.expect: Slippery marble, no shade and heavy crowds from 10 am to 2 pm.
items.tip: Enter at the upper gate at opening and walk downhill to the lower gate.
items.why: It is one of the great ancient sites of the world.
flow: Taxi to the upper gate at 8 am.
Walk down Curetes Street to the library, the theatre and the lower gate.

items.name: Ephesus Terrace Houses
items.summary: Roman villas on the hillside with mosaics and wall paintings, under a protective roof.
items.expect: A separate ticket and glass walkways with many stairs.
items.tip: Do not skip it; most groups do, so it is quiet.
items.why: The best look at how wealthy Romans lived, with decoration still on the walls.
flow: Entrance is opposite Hadrian's Temple on Curetes Street.
Follow the walkway up and out at the top.

items.name: Ephesus Archaeological Museum
items.summary: The finds from Ephesus, including the two marble statues of Artemis.
items.expect: A compact museum that takes about an hour.
items.tip: Visit after the ruins, in the heat of the afternoon.
items.why: It holds what was removed from the site for safekeeping.
flow: Walk from the town centre.
Terrace house finds, then the Artemis hall.

items.name: Basilica of St. John and Ayasuluk Castle
items.summary: The ruins of Justinian's great church over the traditional tomb of John the Apostle, with a castle above.
items.expect: An open hilltop with views to the İsa Bey Mosque and the plain.
items.tip: Come near sunset for the light and the storks nesting on the columns.
items.why: A major early Christian site that few Ephesus day-trippers reach.
flow: Walk up from the town centre.
Basilica, then up to the castle walls.

items.name: Temple of Artemis
items.summary: The site of one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, now a single rebuilt column in a marsh.
items.expect: Very little remains; it is a ten-minute stop.
items.tip: Stop on the walk back from Ephesus to town.
items.why: For the history rather than the view.
flow: Walk from the museum.
Read the panel and look back to the basilica and castle.

items.name: House of the Virgin Mary
items.summary: A small stone chapel in the forest, a place of pilgrimage for Christians and Muslims.
items.expect: A short, quiet visit; modest dress and no photos inside.
items.tip: Share a taxi from the upper gate of Ephesus, 7 km away.
items.why: A peaceful stop with meaning for many visitors.
flow: Taxi from Selçuk or Ephesus.
Chapel, spring and the wishing wall.

items.name: Şirince
items.summary: A hill village of white Greek houses, known for fruit wines and olive oil.
items.expect: Busy on weekends with Turkish day-trippers.
items.tip: Go on a weekday afternoon and stay for dinner.
items.why: A pretty contrast to the ruins, 20 minutes away.
flow: Minibus from Selçuk bus station.
Walk up through the lanes to the church of St. John the Baptist.

items.name: Ejder Restaurant
items.summary: A family-run grill with tables beside the Byzantine aqueduct.
items.expect: Simple, friendly and popular with travellers.
items.tip: Sit outside under the aqueduct arches where storks nest in summer.
items.why: Reliable home cooking in the best spot in town.
flow: Walk from the train station.
Meze, then skewers from the grill.

items.name: Selçuk Köftecisi
items.summary: A no-frills meatball house that has served the same short menu for decades.
items.expect: Busy at lunch with locals.
items.tip: Order köfte with piyaz and the house yoghurt.
items.why: The town's favourite cheap lunch.
flow: Near the market square.
Köfte, bean salad and ayran.

items.name: Artemis Restaurant and Wine House
items.summary: A restaurant in the old village schoolhouse with a terrace over the valley.
items.expect: Large and busy at weekends.
items.tip: Taste the fruit wines before choosing a bottle.
items.why: The view over Şirince's rooftops at sunset.
flow: At the entrance to the village.
Aegean herb meze, then a clay-pot dish.

name: Pamukkale
tagline: White terraces and a Roman spa city
summary: A hillside of white travertine pools with the ruins of Hierapolis on top. One night lets you see it at sunset and again at opening, before the day tours arrive.
seasonNote: Summer midday is blinding and hot on the white rock; winter is cold but the water stays warm and crowds are thin.
arrival: Fly to Denizli (1 hour by shuttle) or take a bus or train to Denizli and a 30-minute minibus to Pamukkale village.
gettingAround: The village and the south gate are on foot. Laodicea and Karahayıt are a short minibus or taxi ride; Aphrodisias needs a car or tour.
cashTip: The village has few ATMs; carry lira for minibuses and small restaurants.
foodTip: Denizli is known for tandır kebabı, slow-roasted lamb eaten with flatbread; village restaurants also do good gözleme.
buyTip: Denizli is Turkey's towel and cotton capital, so buy peştemal towels and bathrobes here.
baseArea: Pamukkale village, within a walk of the lower gate

connections.note: Minibus to Denizli, then train or bus.
From Denizli airport, an hour away.

items.name: Pamukkale travertines
items.summary: A white hillside of calcium terraces and shallow warm pools that you climb barefoot.
items.expect: Shoes off for the whole climb; the surface is ridged and wet, and some pools are dry by rotation.
items.tip: Enter by the lower gate late in the afternoon and walk up for sunset, or be first in at opening.
items.why: There is nothing else like it and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
flow: Enter at the lower gate in the village.
Walk barefoot up the terraces to Hierapolis at the top.

items.name: Hierapolis
items.summary: A Roman spa city above the terraces with a superb theatre and a vast necropolis.
items.expect: Included in the travertine ticket; the site is spread out with little shade.
items.tip: Walk up to the theatre first, then out along the main street to the necropolis.
items.why: The theatre alone would be worth the trip.
flow: From the top of the travertines, climb to the theatre.
Follow Frontinus Street to the north necropolis.

items.name: Cleopatra's Antique Pool
items.summary: A warm thermal pool where you swim over fallen Roman columns.
items.expect: An extra fee, lockers and a busy cafe; crowded at midday.
items.tip: Bring a swimsuit and go before 10 am or after 5 pm.
items.why: A swim among ancient columns in 36°C water.
flow: Inside the Hierapolis site, beside the museum.
Change, swim, then dry off in the garden.

items.name: Hierapolis Archaeology Museum
items.summary: Sarcophagi and sculpture from Hierapolis and Laodicea, displayed in the vaulted Roman baths.
items.expect: Small; half an hour is enough.
items.tip: A cool break in the middle of the day.
items.why: The building is as interesting as the collection.
flow: At the top of the travertines.
Three halls in the old bath house.

items.name: Laodicea on the Lycus
items.summary: A large, recently excavated city with re-erected colonnades and one of the Seven Churches of Revelation.
items.expect: Almost no crowds and active excavation.
items.tip: Stop on the way to or from Denizli; allow an hour and a half.
items.why: A quiet, impressive site that most Pamukkale visitors miss.
flow: Minibus towards Denizli, 15 minutes.
Syria Street, the church, then the two theatres.

items.name: Aphrodisias
items.summary: A city of sculptors with a 30,000-seat stadium, a monumental gateway and an outstanding museum.
items.expect: About 90 minutes each way by road; very few visitors.
items.tip: Hire a car or join a small tour, and leave an hour for the museum's Sebasteion reliefs.
items.why: Many travellers rate it above Ephesus for atmosphere, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
flow: Drive or tour from Pamukkale.
Tetrapylon, stadium, theatre, then the museum.

items.name: Kayaş Restaurant & Bar
items.summary: A long-running village restaurant with a wide menu of Turkish home dishes.
items.expect: Friendly service and a traveller crowd.
items.tip: Ask what was cooked that day rather than ordering from the long menu.
items.why: The most dependable dinner in the village.
flow: On the main street.
Meze, then a casserole or grill.

items.name: Mehmet's Heaven
items.summary: A cushion-floored restaurant with a back terrace facing the travertines.
items.expect: Simple food; you come for the view.
items.tip: Arrive before sunset for a terrace seat.
items.why: The best view of the white hillside from any table in the village.
flow: Near the lower gate.
Order a casserole and watch the terraces turn pink.

items.name: Hiera Coffee & Tea House
items.summary: A small family cafe-restaurant known for home-cooked plates and good coffee.
items.expect: Few tables and unhurried service.
items.tip: Good for breakfast before the opening-time climb.
items.why: The warmest welcome in the village.
flow: A short walk from the lower gate.
Turkish breakfast or a home-style main.

name: Bodrum
tagline: Whitewashed Aegean harbour under a crusader castle
summary: A white harbour town on a peninsula of coves and villages. See the castle and the old town in a day, then spend the rest on a boat, a beach or dinner by the water in Gümüşlük.
seasonNote: July and August are hot, crowded and the most expensive; from November to April much of the peninsula shuts.
arrival: Milas-Bodrum airport is 35 km away; the Havaş bus takes about 45 minutes. Summer ferries run to Kos in 45 minutes.
gettingAround: Dolmuş minibuses fan out from the central station to every village on the peninsula; the old town is on foot.
cashTip: Cards are accepted widely; carry lira for dolmuş fares and beach vendors.
foodTip: Order grilled sea bream or bass, Aegean herb meze, stuffed courgette flowers and çökertme kebabı.
buyTip: Handmade leather sandals are a Bodrum tradition; the Tuesday textile market is the big one.
baseArea: Bodrum town for sights and nightlife; Bitez or Gümüşlük for quiet
via: Direct from Europe in summer; otherwise via Istanbul

connections.note: Direct buses in summer; otherwise change in Söke.

items.name: Bodrum Castle
items.summary: A 15th-century castle of the Knights of St. John that houses the Museum of Underwater Archaeology.
items.expect: Many steps and towers; some halls close for restoration.
items.tip: Do not miss the Uluburun Bronze Age shipwreck hall.
items.why: The landmark of the town and one of the world's best shipwreck museums.
flow: Enter from the harbour side.
Walls, towers, then the shipwreck halls.

items.name: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
items.summary: The foundations of the tomb of Mausolus, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
items.expect: Only foundations, fragments and a model remain.
items.tip: A 30-minute stop; the castle walls contain many of its stones.
items.why: The origin of the word mausoleum.
flow: Walk 10 minutes uphill from the marina.
Model room, then the pit of foundations.

items.name: Bodrum Ancient Theatre
items.summary: A restored Greek theatre on the hillside with a view over the castle and both bays.
items.expect: Beside the main road; free and usually empty.
items.tip: Come for sunset.
items.why: The best view of the town.
flow: Walk up from the Mausoleum.
Climb to the top rows.

items.name: Bodrum old town and marina
items.summary: White cube houses draped in bougainvillea, bazaar lanes and a waterfront of wooden gulets.
items.expect: Lively until late; the bar street east of the castle is loud.
items.tip: Walk the marina west of the castle in the evening.
items.why: The look that made Bodrum famous.
flow: Start at the castle square.
Bazaar lanes, then the marina promenade.

items.name: Gulet boat day around the bays
items.summary: A day on a wooden gulet stopping to swim at Karaada, the Aquarium bay and Camel Beach.
items.expect: Shared boats play music and carry 40 or more; lunch is included.
items.tip: Choose a smaller boat or the route to Orak Island for clearer water.
items.why: The water is the reason to come to Bodrum.
flow: Board in the harbour around 10 am.
Four or five swim stops, back by 5 pm.

items.name: Gümüşlük
items.summary: A fishing village on the site of ancient Myndos, with tables set at the water's edge.
items.expect: No new building is allowed, so it stays low-key; busy for sunset.
items.tip: Wade across the sunken causeway to Rabbit Island, then stay for fish.
items.why: The peninsula's best sunset and seafood dinner.
flow: Dolmuş from Bodrum, 40 minutes.
Swim, wade to the island, dinner by the water.

items.name: Bitez Beach
items.summary: A sheltered, shallow bay lined with beach clubs and tangerine groves.
items.expect: Loungers are free if you order food or drink.
items.tip: A calm option for families and windsurfing beginners.
items.why: The easiest good beach from Bodrum town.
flow: Dolmuş from Bodrum, 15 minutes.
Pick a beach club and settle in.

items.name: Orfoz
items.summary: A small seafood restaurant serving a parade of shellfish tasting plates.
items.expect: A set sequence of small dishes; expensive.
items.tip: Let the kitchen choose and book well ahead in summer.
items.why: Often named among Turkey's best seafood restaurants.
flow: Reserve ahead.
Oysters and clams first, then grilled fish.

items.name: Nazik Ana
items.summary: A canteen-style lokanta where you point at trays of home-cooked dishes.
items.expect: Shared tables and quick turnover; best at lunch.
items.tip: Go before 1 pm for the full choice.
items.why: Honest Turkish home food at local prices in a pricey town.
flow: In a lane behind the bazaar.
Choose at the counter and carry your tray.

items.name: Bodrum Fish Market
items.summary: Lanes where you buy fish from the stalls and have a neighbouring meyhane cook it.
items.expect: Packed, loud and convivial from 8 pm.
items.tip: Agree the fish price by weight and the cooking fee before sitting down.
items.why: The liveliest dinner in town.
flow: Choose your fish at a stall.
Take a table next door and order meze while it grills.
